Steps to Ensure that Sissala West Benefits from Government’s Subsidised Farm Inputs Mr Mohammed Adams Sukparu (NDC — Sissala West): Mr Speaker, I beg to ask the Hon Minister for Food and Agriculture what immediate steps the Ministry is taking to ensure that the good people of Sissala West get Government’s 167 14th February, 2024 168 Oral Answers to Questions subsidised farm inputs for this farming season. 4.4 p.m. Mr B. Acheampong: Mr Speaker, indeed, I have answered this Question through a previous explanation, but as it stands, I would just read the Answer provided by the Ministry. Mr Speaker, prior to the year 2023, farmers in Sissala West district were recipients of direct input subsidies in the form of seeds and fertilisers through the Government's flagship programme, Planting for Food and Jobs (PFJ). However, with the introduction of the second phase of the programme, PFJ Phase II, there has been a notable shift in Government policy. The focus has transitioned from direct input subsidies to an input credit system, wherein all participating farmers will obtain farm inputs on credit facilitated by aggregators. Mr Speaker, the input credit system extends its coverage to include mechanisation and technical support for farmers through extension officers. A significant advantage of this system is that farmers will repay the value of the inputs in kind. This approach not only eases the financial burden on farmers but also liberates resources that would have otherwise been spent on purchasing subsidised inputs. Additionally, farmers enrolled under the PFJ Phase II will benefit from off-taker arrangements, ensuring convenient access to markets. Mr Speaker, this strategic move is poised to address the persistent issue of recurring post-harvest losses, ultimately safeguarding the returns on investment for farmers. Farmers in the Sissala district can, therefore, anticipate government support under PFJ Phase II without any reservations. I thank the Hon Member for his Question and concern. Parliament discussed agriculture-related topics, including:

* The distribution of fertilizers to farmers, with some Members expressing concerns about the procurement process [8fc1281cb1ee366dbcdd5d1c0fc5bc7fe7694f66b15f56486c8e07923dae2e32:121].
* A policy on free distribution of fertilizers and seedlings for cocoa and food crops, but no clear direction on procurement and distribution [cc72c8f414ba98a37132751f20d36ff71cbdc2573138c346017d3018378ff147:53].
* The establishment of Farm Service Centres as one-stop shops for farmers to access agriculture mechanization services, high-quality seeds, fertilizers, and extension services [cc72c8f414ba98a37132751f20d36ff71cbdc2573138c346017d3018378ff147:53].
* The Feed the Industry programme, which aims to establish a strong relationship between agriculture and industry by making agro processors available throughout the year [ac3d47059b7a4c74c6acd64cfd59ca70bc3d6b6bf35b7bbc438440cc9e0ae2e5:5].

Note that these discussions were part of a larger debate on government policies and initiatives related to agriculture, food security, and farming support.
